title: The effect of metformin on inferior alveolar nerve regeneration following crush-type injury
html: Peripheral nerve injuries often cause significant sensory and motor dysfunction, but current treatments provide limited neurosensory recovery. Beyond its antidiabetic use, metformin shows promise as a neuroprotective and regenerative agent by modulating autophagy and reducing inflammation. This study aimed to investigate the potential therapeutic effects of metformin on inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) regeneration following crush-type injury in a rat model. Thirty male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly divided into metformin, placebo, and control groups.
